description:
Benchmarking the AMD Radeon RX 5600 XT against 13 popular and recent games on an average gaming PC in 2023.

As the new graphics card market is bereft of good value options below £150, I’ve been searching for a truly great value option to recommend on the used market, and the RX 56000 XT looks like possibly the ideal card to fill that niche. Recently, the first games have launched that cannot run on hardware that lacks DX12_1 functionality, so my previous recommendations for the RX 480, 580 and 590 are beginning to show their age. With RDNA architecture, a modest amount of VRAM and some impressive specs, is the RX 5600 XT the best budget choice?

I got myself a power color red dragon 5700xt which has been doing very well thus far in terms of temps. comments.text:
@footballartisan8990  I ran a 5700 XT from launch until until 2023. Basically, if you had any driver issues after the 20.2.2 driver, it's not the driver causing problems, it's one of these issues and most commonly in this order of prevalence:
1. Unstable RAM. Most people test their RAM without a load on the GPU. However, the GPU heat soaks your RAM, so you need to test the RAM with the GPU loaded. Radeon drivers are ridiculously sensitive to unstable RAM.
2. Power issues. Make sure you're using 2 separate PCI-E cables running to the PSU and not a single split cable. You'll also want a good quality PSU because while the 5700 XT isn't extremely power hungry, it does have transient swings that momentarily draw 300W+, and a poor quality PSU may not keep up when that happens.
3. The GPU is straight up faulty. Usually it's because of a bad VRAM module, or because traces in the PCB have stress fractures because of a heavy heatsink and GPU sag. At this point, all you can do in this situation is find a business who does component level repair, plan for the repair to cost between $80-$120 and decide if it's worth the cost to do it or to move on.
